Oliver R.: Heads-up: FinServX asking for a Private deployment POC. Key constraints: inference hosts must not have direct internet egress; they need original client source IPs preserved for audit; firewall team requires exact allowlist and an architecture recommendation (PrivateLink vs TGW/peering). Also need a ballpark for Dedicated reserved vs Private license.
Anna S.: Quick clarifier  are they ok with a customer-managed egress proxy (inside their VPC/onprem) that handles all outbound traffic to security tooling, or do they want literally zero outbound to internet from inference nodes (control plane only via private connectivity)?
Oliver R.: They said zero internet egress from model hosts. Control plane allowed over PrivateLink OR via a transit path to our control plane endpoints. They want port/IP snippets for firewall, and a fast cost estimate to sign PO.
Marc P.: Architecture notes: PrivateLink (VPC Interface Endpoints) is simplest for strict allowlists: customer allows traffic to the vpce ENI IPs and SGs. Downside: PrivateLink does not preserve original client source IP to the service. TGW/peering (route-based) can preserve source IP if our deployment is attached as a VPC behind the TGW or if customer deploys a pass-through appliance. TGW is more flexible but requires route table and possibly an NVA for inspection.
Jai N.: Source-IP preservation options: (1) TGW + our VPC attachment where traffic flows without SNAT -> preserves src IP; (2) customer-managed proxy (e.g., envoy) that forwards X-Forwarded-For and avoids NAT; (3) If PrivateLink is used, client src becomes the endpoint ENI IP so original src is lost unless you add an application layer header. 
Sarah L.: Compliance needs: confirm SOC2 scope covers Private deployment; recommend logs be written to customer-controlled S3 and integrate KMS for key management. Need to confirm HSM/FIPS requirement. Also note retention window for audit logs and whether traces leave the customer VPC.
Anna S.: Minimal firewall allowlist (examples):

- Control plane (PrivateLink): TCP 443 -> vpce-<id> (PrivateLink endpoint)
- Model serving (internal between app and inference pool): TCP 8443 (gRPC), health/probes TCP 10256
- Optional metrics scraping: TCP 9090/9091 to metrics collector if they want central scraping

Sample security group snippet: 
```
# Allow app subnet -> inference pool
Type: TCP
Port: 8443
Source: 10.60.0.0/20  # customer app subnet

# Outbound from inference nodes -> control plane via vpce or proxy
Type: HTTPS
Port: 443
Destination: vpce-0abc123def456  # example PrivateLink vpce id
```

Marc P.: If they must keep client IP in server logs, advise TGW + VPC attachment or a lightweight sidecar proxy on the app side that inserts X-Forwarded-For. Sidecar adds small latency (~30-70ms depending on config).
Jai N.: TGW route example (minimal):
```
# in customer route table for app subnet
0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-gw (if egress) or specific route to tgw-attach-id for service subnets
# route for service subnet -> target: tgw-attach-id
```
Note: don't rely on FQDN-based allowlists for PrivateLink; prefer IP/ENI-based allowlists. If they insist on FQDN, use their proxy to resolve and allow the internal LB FQDN we provide.
Oliver R.: Pricing ballpark request for 2-node POC (24/7, mid-tier GPUs) + Private deployment license?
Anna S.: Rough sticker: Dedicated reserved (2 mid GPUs) ~ $12k/month; Private deployment platform license ~ $6k/month; combined conservative POC estimate ~ $18k/month. Include note: final price depends on GPU class, data egress handling, and support tier.
Sarah L.: I'll draft a compliance checklist: SOC2 scope confirmation, KMS integration steps, HSM/FIPS callout, log retention & S3 path, and whether we can ship audit logs to customer's logging endpoint.
Marc P.: I'll produce a one-page diagram (PrivateLink variant and TGW variant) + annotated pros/cons and a clear allowlist snippet for each.
Jai N.: I'll validate SG rules and route table examples and add a minimal TGW config to hand to their network ops.
Anna S.: I'll update pricing sheet and include licensing/support note and PO checklist.
Oliver R.: Perfect. Please have the deliverables ready by EOD tomorrow; FinServX wants security ops signoff Wed 10am PT. Ping me when done.
